text:
jade: Quick sync — noticed a reproducible cross-node 'drift' when handing back GPU pages to host under heavy offload. runc-12, batch size 16, spikes at ~1200 req/s. Anyone seen similar?

kyle: seen weird residency mismatches, but not cross-node. what do you mean by 'drift'? page shows up on wrong host?

jade: yeah, pages get returned but residency metadata still claims GPU A. Next inference that touches it faults, causing a remote copy + extra latency. repro steps below.

marta: oof. could be race between the offload ACK and the lease revocation path. do you have a traceback or logs?

jade: pasted a minimal trace — note timings and the host id mismatch.

eli: sharing perf counters from runc-12 during the repro:
```
offload_ack: t=161234.752
lease_release: t=161234.753
residency_update: t=161234.754 host=GPU_A
fault_on_touch: t=161234.762 observed_host=GPU_B
```
```
vmmap: [0x7f1a..] -> gpu_a_backing (refcount 0)
page_meta: owner=tenant-17 pool=staging host=GPU_A last_touch=161234.740
```

kyle: that looks like a window where a followup binder/handback raced with a migration. Maybe the handback path clears the GPU mapping but the residency table update is non-atomic w/ migration token.

marta: Could also be caused by our async return path that batches ACKs. If the ACK bundler reorders messages, lease manager might process them out of order.

jade: exactly — repro happens when bundler is enabled and bundling is small. disabling bundler makes it disappear in our tests.

eli: hypothesis: ACK bundler buffers release notices and sends them in bulk. If a migration happens in between, we can get: migrate->ack-bundle-send of earlier release, which then marks page resident incorrectly.

kyle: two possible fixes: make residency updates tied to migration tokens (stronger ordering) OR make bundler attach sequencer numbers so lease manager can drop stale messages. I prefer sequencer — lower perf hit.

marta: sequencer seems reasonable. we'll need a small metadata field: seq_id per page op, monotonic per-allocator. If lease manager sees seq_id < current, drop. cheap check.

jade: agree. also add a fast-path check in the fault path to avoid the remote-copy if we detect conflicting metadata, return retry to caller so runtime can re-run with correct view.

kyle: can prototype seq_id as u32 in the page_meta. quick patch idea:
```
diff --git a/page_meta.h b/page_meta.h
+ uint32_t seq_id; // monotonic per-alloc
```
and in bundler: attach seq_id = ++alloc->last_seq; in lease consume: if (incoming.seq_id < meta.seq_id) ignore.

marta: watch out for wraparound on u32; just increment and use (incoming - meta) signed check. Also think about persisted snapshots during migration.

eli: also add a short TTL for seq validity in distributed runs — if we see a seq delta > 1e7 treat as ambiguous (likely restart) and force sync.

jade: sounds good. experiment plan: 1) land seq_id check only (no bundler change) 2) run soak on runc-12 for 24h with load-replay tool 3) if stable, enable seq attach in bundler and re-run.

kyle: I'll put up a draft PR with tests for ordering and a small benchmark to measure impact on hot path (~should be negligible).

marta: I'll add an integration test that purposely reorders bundles and assert lease manager drops stale updates.

eli: I'll run the repro harness and collect traces. also will add a debug flag to log seq numbers for a short window.

ops-bot: CI queued — build/allocator-seq-check (linux, amd64) #4821 started by kyle

jade: thanks everyone. quick note — if we do seq_id, update any tooling that scrapes page_meta in telemetry so alerts don't freak out.

kyle: noted. will also add a migration-e2e flake guard.

marta: one more thought: if we add seq_id, consider using it in compaction to avoid coalescing pages with mismatched histories. not required now but FYI.

jade: action items: kyle PR, marta integration test, eli traces. follow up EOD here. :thumbsup:
